newsitem.title: USA: Kmart improved sales boost Q2 profits.
newsitem.headline: Kmart improved sales boost Q2 profits.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Thursday higher sales in most merchandise categories thus far this year boosted 1997 second quarter operating profits.
Sales of housewares and home decor, cosmetics and fragrances, and consumables showed strength, said Floyd Hall, chairman, president and chief executive officer.

Kmart reported net income from continuing operations rose to $31 million or $0.06 a share in the second quarter of 1997 from net income from continuing operations in the second quarter of 1996 of $23 million or $0.05 a share.

Total sales in the second quarter were $7.85 billion, an increase of 3.7 percent from $7.57 billion from the second quarter of 1996. On a comparable store basis, consolidated sales for the quarter increased 5.5 percent.
"Sales in our U.S. Kmart stores increased 5.6 percent on a comparable store basis for the first six months of 1996, which meets our expectations," Hall said in a news release.

"Strong sales also helped expense ratios, which improved by 120 basis points in the second quarter. Total spending on SG&A improved both in the quarter and over the first half of 1997, totaling $70 million year-to-date," he said.

Gross margin rates for the second quarter were depressed by clearance of slow-moving inventory. He said the company has been disappointed by the volume and margin in its women's apparel to date, but is entering the third quarter with seasonal inventory levels below last year, and it expects improved softline performance in the second half of 1997.
Kmart operates 2,122 Kmart, Big Kmart, and Super Kmart retail outlets.
